en: to lecture (in class); to teach a course

examples.en: The professor lectures every Monday.
She taught Korean at a university.
The way he lectures is fun.
To teach online, you need a camera.
The topic I will lecture on is Hangul.
I took questions after lecturing.

explain: 대학이나 학원에서 길게 가르칠 때 써요. 학교 수업은 보통 '수업'이라고 하고 가르치는 일은 '가르치다'라고 해요. 듣는 사람은 '강의를 듣다'라고 말해요.

phrases.en: The professor gives a lecture this afternoon.
phrases.nuance_ko: '강의하다'와 같은 뜻이고 조금 더 풀어서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '강의하다', phrased in a slightly longer way.

phrases.en: I take a Korean lecture every week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 강의를 하는 사람이 아니라 듣는 학생의 입장에서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said from the view of the student who listens, not the lecturer.

explain_en: Used for teaching at length at a university or academy. School classes are usually '수업', and teaching in general is '가르치다'. The listener says '강의를 듣다'.

examples.en: As the sun set, the sky turned golden.
I saw a child with golden hair.
The autumn fields are golden.

examples.ko: 저녁 햇살의 금빛은 사진에 잘 담기지 않아요.
examples.en: The golden color of evening sunlight doesn't come out well in photos.
Golden leaves blow in the wind.
I received a ring with a golden tint as a gift.

explain: 금처럼 빛나는 노란색을 말할 때 써요. '금색'과 비슷하지만 '-빛'이 붙어서 빛나는 느낌이 더 있어요. 노을, 머리카락, 곡식 밭처럼 풍경을 그릴 때 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: I got a gold ring as a gift.
phrases.nuance_ko: 금빛과 비슷하지만 물건의 색을 말할 때 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 금빛, but more common for the color of objects.

phrases.en: The golden field is beautiful in autumn.
phrases.nuance_ko: 곡식이 익은 풍경을 그릴 때 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits well when describing ripe grain fields.

phrases.en: The evening sea shines golden.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빛이 비쳐서 반짝이는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes something sparkling in golden light.

explain_en: Use it for a shiny, gold-like yellow. It is close to '금색', but the '-빛' ending adds a feeling of shining light. It suits scenery such as sunsets, hair, and grain fields.

en: to be divided; to be split

examples.en: The cake was divided into six pieces.
Our class splits into two teams.
If opinions split in two, we vote.
It is important that profits are shared fairly.
The room is divided by a curtain.

examples.ko: 열 개는 둘로 똑같이 나누어질 수 있어요.
examples.en: Ten items can be split evenly into two.

explain: 말할 때는 줄여서 '나뉘다'라고 더 자주 해요. '나뉘어요', '나뉘었어요'처럼요. '나누다'는 내가 직접 가르는 행동이고, '나누어지다'는 저절로 또는 어떤 이유로 갈라진 상태예요.

phrases.en: Our class is divided into three teams.
phrases.nuance_ko: '나누어져요'를 줄인 말로, 말할 때 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The shortened form of 나누어져요, more common in speech.

phrases.en: People's opinions were split in two.
phrases.nuance_ko: 생각이나 의견이 갈라졌을 때도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can also be used when opinions or views split.

phrases.example: 사탕이 일곱 개라서 둘로 똑같이 나누어지지 않아요.
phrases.en: There are seven candies, so they can't be split equally between two.
phrases.nuance_ko: 똑같이 나눌 수 없을 때 부정형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, used when something can't be split equally.

explain_en: In speech it is often shortened to 나뉘다, as in 나뉘어요 and 나뉘었어요. 나누다 is something you do yourself, while 나누어지다 describes something that ends up split, on its own or for some reason.

dis.h: be divided; common, full everyday form

p.n: Same meaning; 나뉘다 is the shorter form of 나누어지다.

examples.en: I was furious, but I held it in.
I got soaked in the rain from head to toe.

examples.ko: 키가 커서 머리끝이 천장에 닿을 것 같아요.
examples.en: I'm so tall that the top of my head almost touches the ceiling.

examples.ko: 그 말을 들으니 머리끝이 쭈뼛 섰어요.
examples.en: Hearing that made the hair on my head stand on end.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 머리끝에서 발끝까지 흰옷을 입고 있었어요.
examples.en: That person was dressed in white from head to toe.
The child pulled the blanket over his head and hid.

explain: '머리끝부터 발끝까지'처럼 '발끝'과 짝으로 써서 온몸을 말해요. 머리 위 한가운데를 정확히 가리킬 때는 '정수리'라고 해요. 화가 크게 났을 때 쓰는 표현도 있어요.

phrases.example: 동생이 약속을 어겨서 머리끝까지 화가 났어요.
phrases.en: be furious
phrases.nuance_ko: 참기 어려울 만큼 몹시 화가 날 때 써요. 실제로 머리에서 화가 난다는 뜻이 아니라 화가 가득 찼다는 과장이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you are so angry you can hardly hold it in. It is an exaggeration meaning anger fills you up, not about the head itself.

phrases.example: 무서운 이야기를 듣고 머리끝이 쭈뼛 섰어요.
phrases.en: I heard a scary story and my hair stood on end.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갑자기 몹시 무섭거나 놀랐을 때 써요. 실제로 머리카락이 서는 것이 아니라 소름이 돋을 만큼 겁이 났다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you are suddenly very scared or startled. It means you got chills of fear, not that your hair literally stands up.
phrases.en_equiv: make your hair stand on end

explain_en: It pairs with '발끝' in '머리끝부터 발끝까지' to mean the whole body. To point exactly to the crown of the head, you say '정수리'. There is also an expression that uses it for being very angry.

en: to pour out; to be brought out

examples.en: When class ended, the students poured out through the school gate.
After the show ends, the audience pours out all at once.
They say people are pouring out into the streets to see the fireworks.

examples.ko: 지하철 문이 열리자 사람들이 몰려나오기 시작했어요.
examples.en: When the subway doors opened, people began to pour out.
The sight of children rushing out to the playground is cute.
Fans will pour out when the game ends, so let's hurry.

explain: 여러 사람이 한꺼번에 나올 때 쓰고, 한 사람이 나올 때는 쓰지 않아요. 반대로 안으로 들어올 때는 '몰려들다', 이쪽으로 올 때는 '몰려오다'를 써요. '학생들이', '관객들이'처럼 여러 명을 나타내는 주어와 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: When the workday ends, people all pour out at once.
phrases.nuance_ko: '한꺼번에'를 넣어 많은 사람이 동시에 나온다는 느낌을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '한꺼번에' stresses that many people come out together.

phrases.en: It's the time when students pour out in front of the school.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는'을 붙여 뒤에 오는 명사를 꾸며요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-는' lets it describe the noun that follows.

phrases.example: 경기가 끝나자 사람들이 경기장에서 쏟아져 나왔어요.
phrases.en: When the game ended, people poured out of the stadium.
phrases.nuance_ko: '몰려나오다'와 비슷하게 많은 사람이 나올 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '몰려나오다' for a crowd coming out.

explain_en: It is used when many people come out at once, not for a single person. For crowds going inside you use '몰려들다', and for coming toward you '몰려오다'. It often takes plural subjects such as '학생들이' or '관객들이'.

examples.ko: 어두운 방에 혼자 있으니 무서움이 밀려왔어요.
examples.en: Being alone in the dark room, fear washed over me.
I turned on the light to overcome my fear.

examples.ko: 아이는 무서움에 떨며 엄마 곁에 붙어 있었어요.
examples.en: The child clung to its mother, trembling with fear.
Fear is a feeling everyone has.
The movie was so fun that I even forgot my fear.

examples.ko: 그는 무서움 없이 혼자 숲으로 들어갔어요.
examples.en: He went into the forest alone without any fear.

explain: '무서움을 느끼다', '무서움을 이기다'처럼 써요. '무섭다'에서 나온 명사예요. 무서움은 귀신, 어둠, 높은 곳처럼 눈앞의 것이 무서울 때 쓰고, '두려움'은 앞으로 일어날 일이 걱정될 때도 써서 범위가 더 넓어요.

phrases.example: 동생은 무서움을 많이 타서 밤에 혼자 화장실에 못 가요.
phrases.en: be easily frightened
phrases.nuance_ko: 겁이 많아서 쉽게 무서워하는 사람을 말할 때 써요. 여기서 '타다'는 그런 느낌을 잘 받는다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for someone who gets scared easily. Here '타다' means being prone to that feeling.

explain_en: It goes with '무서움을 느끼다' and '무서움을 이기다', and it is the noun form of '무섭다'. 무서움 is for something scary right in front of you, like ghosts, the dark or heights, while '두려움' is wider and also covers worry about what may happen.

en: to reflect (light or sound) off a surface

examples.en: The mirror reflects sunlight.
The lake reflected the sky.
The window reflected light and it was dazzling.
White is a color that reflects a lot of light.

examples.ko: 산이 소리를 반사하기 때문에 메아리가 들려요.
examples.en: The mountain reflects sound, which is why you hear an echo.
Light reflected from the wall hit my face.

explain: 빛이나 소리가 되돌아가게 할 때 써요. 피동 '반사되다'도 자주 써서 '빛이 거울에 반사돼요'처럼 말해요. 몸이 저절로 반응하는 '반사 신경'이라는 말도 있어요.

phrases.en: The wall reflects sound, so it echoes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빛뿐 아니라 소리에도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for sound as well as light.

phrases.en: Light reflects off the water and it's dazzling.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반사되는 쪽을 주어로 말할 때 '반사되다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form is used when the light is the subject.

phrases.en: The glass that reflects sunlight is dazzling.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 오는 명사를 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to modify a noun that follows.

explain_en: It is used when light or sound bounces back. The passive '반사되다' is also common, as in '빛이 거울에 반사돼요' (light is reflected in the mirror). The same noun appears in '반사 신경' (reflexes).

examples.ko: 할머니는 길고양이를 불쌍히 여겨서 밥을 줬어요.
examples.en: Grandmother felt sorry for the stray cat and gave it food.

examples.ko: 힘든 사람을 불쌍히 여기는 마음은 누구에게나 있어요.
examples.en: Everyone has a heart that feels pity for people who are struggling.

examples.ko: 저를 불쌍히 여기지 마세요, 저는 괜찮아요.
examples.en: Please don't pity me, I'm fine.

examples.ko: 부디 이 아이들을 불쌍히 여겨 주세요.
examples.en: Please take pity on these children.

examples.ko: 모두가 그 사정을 듣고 그를 불쌍히 여겼어요.
examples.en: Everyone heard his situation and felt sorry for him.

examples.ko: 남을 불쌍히 여길 줄 아는 사람이 되고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to be a person who knows how to feel pity for others.

explain: '불쌍히 여기다'처럼 거의 '여기다'와 같이 써요. 다른 동사 앞에서는 보통 '불쌍하게'를 써서 '불쌍하게 울다'라고 해요. 상대에게 동정하는 마음이 담겨서, 듣는 사람이 기분 나빠할 수도 있어요.

phrases.example: 강아지가 비를 맞고 불쌍하게 떨고 있어요.
phrases.en: The puppy is shivering pitifully in the rain.
phrases.nuance_ko: '불쌍히'와 달리 여러 동사 앞에 자유롭게 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Unlike 불쌍히, it can go before many different verbs.

phrases.en: The child who was alone looked pitiful.
phrases.nuance_ko: 보기에 안타깝다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone looks sad to see.

phrases.en: He doesn't feel pity for others.
phrases.nuance_ko: '불쌍히 여기다'를 부정하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form of 불쌍히 여기다.

explain_en: It is used almost only with '여기다', as in '불쌍히 여기다'. Before other verbs people usually say '불쌍하게', as in '불쌍하게 울다'. It carries a feeling of pity toward someone, which can make the listener uncomfortable.

examples.en: I do the sketch first and then add color.
The sketch is so simple that I cannot tell what it is.
I drew a few sketches in my notebook.
I do the sketch lightly with a pencil.
I will add color to this sketch.
I will show you a sketch first.

explain: '밑그림'은 색을 칠하기 전에 밑바탕으로 그리는 그림이고, '스케치'는 대상을 보고 빠르게 그린 그림 자체에도 써요. '여행 스케치'처럼 가볍게 그린 그림 이름으로도 붙어요.

phrases.en: I sketched a tree in the park.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빠르게 대상을 그린다는 동사로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb for quickly drawing a subject.

phrases.example: 밑그림을 먼저 그린 다음에 색을 칠해요.
phrases.en: I draw the base sketch first and then paint it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 색을 칠하기 전에 그리는 바탕 그림을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The base drawing made before adding color.

phrases.en: I collected my travel sketches and made them into a book.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여행하면서 가볍게 그린 그림 이름으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for light drawings made while traveling.

explain_en: A '밑그림' is the underdrawing made before adding color, while '스케치' can also be a quick drawing of something you see, kept as a piece in itself. It also appears in names like '여행 스케치' for lightly drawn pictures.

examples.en: Have you ever seen a galaxy in the night sky?
There are a great many stars in our galaxy.

examples.ko: 은하 사진을 보니 우주가 넓게 느껴져요.
examples.en: Looking at galaxy photos, the universe feels vast.

examples.ko: 두 은하가 서로 가까이 지나가는 모습이 찍혔어요.
examples.en: An image captured two galaxies passing close to each other.
The shape of this galaxy looks like a spiral.

examples.ko: 저 은하에서 지구까지 빛이 오는 데 얼마나 걸릴까요?
examples.en: How long does light take to reach Earth from that galaxy?

explain: '은하'는 별이 아주 많이 모인 큰 무리이고, 우리가 사는 곳은 '우리 은하'예요. 밤하늘에 길게 보이는 하얀 띠는 '은하수'라고 불러요.

phrases.en: Our galaxy has a great many stars.
phrases.nuance_ko: 우리가 사는 지구가 속한 은하를 가리킬 때는 '우리'를 앞에 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put '우리' before it to mean the galaxy that Earth belongs to.

phrases.en: I saw the Milky Way for the first time in the countryside.
phrases.nuance_ko: '은하'는 별 무리이고, '은하수'는 밤하늘에 하얀 띠처럼 보이는 모습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: '은하' is the star system itself; '은하수' is the pale band seen in the night sky.

phrases.en: I took a photo of a galaxy with a telescope.
phrases.nuance_ko: '은하'를 다른 말 앞에 붙여서 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: '은하' can be placed before another noun.

explain_en: A '은하' is a huge cluster of stars, and the one we live in is '우리 은하' (our galaxy). The long white band seen across the night sky is called '은하수' (the Milky Way).

en: to be concentrated on; to be devoted to

examples.en: People's attention is focused on one place.
The population is concentrated in Seoul.

examples.ko: 힘이 한 사람에게 집중되면 문제가 생겨요.
examples.en: When power is concentrated in one person, problems arise.
Everyone's eyes were on one person.
It is news that will draw attention.
All eyes were on me, so I felt a little shy.

explain: '집중하다'는 사람이 하는 일이고 '집중되다'는 관심, 시선, 인구, 힘이 한쪽에 모일 때 써요. '관심이 집중되다', '시선이 집중되다'가 자주 쓰는 짝이에요.

phrases.en: All the attention is focused on that player.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation.

phrases.en: Everyone's eyes were focused on the stage.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람들이 한곳을 쳐다볼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when many people look at the same place.

phrases.en: On weekends people crowd to the beach.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이나 일이 한곳에 모일 때 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy word for people or tasks gathering in one place.

explain_en: The active form is a person focusing; this passive is for attention, gazes, population or power gathering in one place. 'Attention is focused' and 'gazes are focused' are the usual pairs.

examples.ko: 흑설탕을 넣으면 커피가 더 진하고 달아요.
examples.en: If you add brown sugar, the coffee becomes richer and sweeter.

examples.ko: 빵 반죽에 흑설탕 한 숟가락을 넣었어요.
examples.en: I put a spoonful of brown sugar into the bread dough.
Brown sugar is darker in color than white sugar.

examples.ko: 겨울에는 흑설탕 넣은 따뜻한 차를 자주 마셔요.
examples.en: In winter I often drink warm tea with brown sugar.
I bought brown sugar and flour at the supermarket.
There is brown sugar inside hotteok.

explain: 반대되는 말은 '백설탕'이에요. 음료 이름에서는 '흑당'이라는 말도 자주 봐요.

phrases.example: 차에 흑설탕 한 숟가락을 넣어 마셔요.
phrases.en: I put a spoonful of brown sugar in my tea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 양을 말할 때 '한 숟가락'과 자주 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often paired with 'a spoonful' to give the amount.

phrases.en: Try using brown sugar instead of white sugar.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대말 '백설탕'과 비교해서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to compare with its opposite, white sugar.
phrases.en_equiv: brown sugar instead of white sugar

phrases.en: I like brown sugar milk tea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음료 이름에서 많이 쓰는 비슷한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word often seen in drink names.

explain_en: Its opposite is '백설탕' (white sugar). On drink menus you will also often see the word '흑당'.
